name: reboot_emlp1_faithful
source: the official ReBoot subset run on quadruped-gpu, as plain values published by gpu-runner (results/quadruped/raw/reboot_emlp1_official_subset/reboot_config_values.json, reboot_subsample_indices.txt, stats.json; no ReBoot source): lr 5e-4 constant, momentum 0.9 (Nesterov SGD), weight decay 0, bias=False, 16 outputs, Xavier uniform init, batch 48, 21 steps, 1 epoch; test accuracy 0.7506
lr_conversion: ReBoot's per-sample loss is sum_k (y_k - y_hat_k)^2 over the 16 outputs, but its implemented output delta is y_hat - y (no factor 2; reboot_config_values.json) and the weight gradient sums over the batch (no 1/B). hekit's delta is a - y and its gradient is the batch mean, so the same step needs lr_mean = lr_sum * B (no factor 2): 0.016 at B = 32, 0.032 at B = 64, 0.024 at B = 48. Checked against ReBoot's 21 per-step batch losses with the exact batches (mnist --mode plain --faithful --batch 48 --indices ...): over 8 init seeds the log-loss rms is 0.048 with factor 1 and 0.091 with factor 2 (last-5-step mean loss 28.1 and 24.7 against ReBoot's 27.4). mnist --lr-sum 5e-4 applies it.
output_width_note: 10 classes padded to 16 rows with zero targets (one-hot padded with zeros), as ReBoot does. The padded rows are trained toward 0 and their deltas reach the hidden layer, so they change the training; the accuracy is the argmax over the 10 real classes. The Xavier bound of layer 2 uses fan_out 16. hekit's layout pads 10 to 16 anyway, so the key-switch counts are unchanged.
subsample_note: ReBoot trains 21 batches of 48 (1008 of the first 1024 training images, shuffled with seed 42; 16 dropped). mnist --indices <file> with gpu-runner's per-step index list trains exactly those samples in that order; without it hekit uses the first 1024 in file order.

seeds.hekit_init: ChaCha20 from mnist --seed (default 32): the initial weights are not ReBoot's draw

input_note: This file is the 784-input subset setting of ReBoot's training_encrypted.py (supplementary rows). The paper's eMLP-1 (Table 2) and ReBoot's full setting use 14 x 14 MNIST: 196 -> 32 -> 10 (16 padded), ruling R-M3-13; run it with the same flags plus --dataset-npy <gpu-runner's 14 x 14 arrays> (the input dimension follows the data; d_in 196 pads to 256, so B up to 128 fits one ciphertext).
